sources.entry: KeyEcho - Plays recorded mechanical keyboard sounds as you type.

summary.one_liner: KeyEcho is a small open-source desktop app that plays recorded mechanical keyboard sounds as you type.
summary.what_it_does: KeyEcho runs as a desktop app and plays keyboard sound effects in response to your key presses. It handles global key events locally and maps them to sound playback, without uploading typed content. The README says it is built with Tauri, Rust, and Solid, with cross-platform builds for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It supports custom sound packs, and a custom sounds guide describes recording, processing, and adding your own packs. Optional paid "Crafted Packs" are mentioned as one-time purchases, but the app itself is described as free and open source and does not require them. Development uses pnpm and Cargo, with scripts for frontend dev, Rust tests, and Tauri production builds.
use_cases: Add mechanical keyboard typing sounds to everyday typing
Create custom keyboard sound packs from my own recordings
Run a lightweight local typing-sound app on Windows, macOS, or Linux
Tune the feel of typing with different sound packs
Build KeyEcho from source for development
notable: Local-only keyboard event handling with no account, cloud sync, or typing-content analytics
Custom sound pack support with a documented recording and processing guide
Small native footprint instead of a bundled browser runtime
Prebuilt downloads for Windows x64/ARM64, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon, and Linux x64/ARM64
caveats: Requires operating system permissions for global keyboard event listening
Optional Crafted Packs are paid ($3.99 each or $9.99 for All Sounds Forever), with paid packs unlocked by a license key
